issues.text: You walked ten thousand steps. Every day. For a year. That's like walking from London... all the way to Moscow.

issues.text: This is K R's What If Explained. I went through nine studies for this one. First of January. You work at a desk. Your phone says you walk about five thousand steps a day. That's normal.

issues.text: Day one. Six p.m. Your phone says... two thousand eight hundred.

issues.text: In the nineteen sixties, a Japanese company needed a catchy name for a new pedometer. Manpo-kei. The ten thousand step meter. Why ten thousand?

issues.text: Month one. Three hundred thousand steps. You step on the weighing scale...
issues.heard: month one 300000 steps you step on the weighing scale

issues.text: Month three. You don't take the lift anymore. You take phone calls walking. And your bad days... feel less bad. A huge Lancet review in twenty twenty-five pulled together fifty-seven studies.

issues.text: No. Because the thing that changed most... was never on the scale. In twenty eleven, scientists in the US had a hundred and twenty older adults walk for a year. Then they scanned their brains.

issues.text: The hippocampus, the part that makes your memories... had grown about two percent. In the group that only stretched... it shrank.

issues.text: Remember pacing your bedroom near midnight? Now ten thousand just... happens. You're simply out for a walk.

issues.text: But after that year, something inside you really does grow. Just not where you'd look. Full video on K R's What If Explained.
